name: Three Colts Tavern (Glue Factory)
summary: A pub on Cambridge Heath Road, run by Exale Brewing, that calls itself a modern East End pub. Its events include quizzes, DJ sets, drag bingo, stand-up and live music.

music.notes: A fortnightly Brazilian choro jam, stand-up and open-spot comedy, a fortnightly quiz, and DJ nights including an alt 80s night played on vinyl.

story.opened: June 2019, as the Fugitive Motel café-bar; it became the Three Colts Tavern under Exale Brewing in 2023.
story.then: Time Out reported in May 2019 that the Fugitive Motel was due to open that June as an all-day café-bar. In January 2023 Beer Today reported that Walthamstow's Exale Brewing was opening a neighbourhood pub on the site, as the Three Colts Tavern. The venue's own website says the building stands where an earlier Three Colts pub was pulled down in 1902, and that the new pub hopes to bring back a little of what was lost.
story.now: The venue's own website says the pub is open seven days a week with a kitchen run by Short Road Pizza, and hosts quizzes, DJs, live music and comedy. There is a shuffleboard table that can be booked by the hour, and the Glue Factory is its private party space.
story.vibe: Beer Today described the building, ahead of its opening in 2023, as having plenty of natural light, exposed concrete and mid-century woodwork, with a lot of outdoor seating. The venue's own website pitches it as a traditional pub in a modern setting.
worth_knowing: The venue's own website says dogs are welcome and that it takes card payments only.
Step-free access runs throughout, according to the venue's own website, apart from the Glue Factory party space, which is up three steps and has no ramp.
The venue's own website says its kitchen partner, Short Road Pizza, was named London's number one pizza by Time Out.

story_research.note: Opened/then/now/vibe/worth_knowing written from the venue site, Time Out (2019) and Beer Today (2023). No post-2023 press review found; the vibe rests on a pre-opening description. Could try Time Out/Evening Standard reviews of the Three Colts.
